title: Rules of the road
intro: Already approved. These are extra ways to say each one, sharper and more you. Keep yours or swap one in.

items.label: 01 · Go someplace new.
items.now: The places you already love will keep. Go and meet one you don't know yet.
alts: Nostalgia is a nice place to visit. Don't book it every year.
Your favourite beach will still be there. That's the beauty of favourites.
Go back when you're old. Go somewhere new while your knees still work.

items.label: 02 · It's what's around the corner.
items.now: The best thing I've seen on any trip was never on the itinerary. It was just past it.
alts: The itinerary gets you there. The corner is why you went.
Every great story I tell starts with 'we took a wrong turn.'
Plans get you to the trailhead. Curiosity gets you to the view.

items.label: 03 · Search on a whim.
items.now: Half my best trips started with “what's that?” and a finger on a map.
alts: The best planning tool I own is the question 'what's over there?'
A whim is just a trip that hasn't met its paperwork yet.
Point at the map. I'll tell you if your finger has good taste.

items.label: 04 · Go on your own, at least once.
items.now: Travel alone and the place does the talking. Travel in a crowd and you mostly hear the crowd.
alts: Eat at the bar alone once. You'll leave with three friends and a better tip than any guidebook.
Alone, nobody argues about dinner. The place picks for you.
Solo travel: the only trip where the person in charge always agrees with you.

items.label: 05 · Leave a few days unplanned.
items.now: Plan the bones. Wing the rest.
alts: A day with nothing on it is the only one nobody can cancel.
Book the flights. Leave the Tuesdays alone.
Empty days fill themselves. Usually better than I could.

items.label: 06 · Last minute can be the best minute.
items.now: Some of the best rooms come free the week before. It helps to know who to call.
alts: Spontaneity is mostly good contacts and a short fuse.
Last minute isn't reckless if someone picks up the phone on the first ring.
The week before is when lodges get honest about their empty rooms.

items.label: 07 · Make mistakes. Just not the expensive ones.
items.now: Forty-four years on the road buys you a long list of wrong turns. I took them so you can take better ones.
alts: I've made most of the mistakes on this page. Consider it a refund.
Experience is just a polite word for every wrong turn I didn't repeat.
Make the cheap mistakes. I already paid for the expensive ones.

title: Mistakes worth skipping: the quips
intro: Approved too. Here are other punchlines for the same five mistakes.

items.label: Seeing a whole country in a week.
items.now: You'll see the airports beautifully.
alts: You'll come home with photos of transfer vans.
Countries don't speed up because you did.

items.label: Changing hotels every night.
items.now: That isn't a trip. It's a check-in tour.
alts: You'll know every lobby and no view.
By night four you're unpacking in your sleep.

items.label: Packing for the big plane when the small one takes you in.
items.now: Bush planes weigh your bag, and they mean it.
alts: The pilot doesn't negotiate. Soft bag, fifteen kilos, smile.
Your hard case can follow you by road. In about a week.

items.label: Filling every hour.
items.now: The sighting you remember happens in the hour you didn't book.
alts: If you schedule the sunset, you'll be in a van for it.
Leave the hour open. The leopard doesn't read your PDF.

items.label: Trusting the brochure photo.
items.now: Which is why everything in the Ledger has been slept in first.
alts: Wide-angle lenses have built more pools than contractors.
The photo was taken in the one week it didn't rain. We went in the other fifty-one.

title: Why it made the Ledger
intro: New. Short reasons stamped on an entry, the real ones a guy who's been there would give. Use them only on places they're true for.
where: Stay pages, beside the founder mark

items.line: Slept here. Would again.
The guide saw the tracks before we saw the road.
They knew my coffee order by the second morning.
Nothing on their website was exaggerated. That alone is rare.
Breakfast outlasted lunch, and nobody minded.
Didn't check my phone for two days. Didn't notice.
The view beat the photographs. That almost never happens.
Worth every bump on the road in.
Came for two nights. Should have booked four.
The owner still answers the phone.

title: Why it didn't make the Ledger
intro: New. The reasons we pass on a place, said the way you'd say them at the bar. For a 'how we vet' page, never naming the hotel.

items.line: Beautiful photographs. Different hotel.
More rules than rooms.
Great spa. The guide couldn't find an elephant in a zoo.
Lovely lodge, wrong side of the river.
Everyone was very nice. Nobody was in charge.
A fine place to stay. Not a reason to fly there.
The Wi-Fi was excellent. That was the highlight.
Three transfers for one afternoon of wild.
The menu had more adjectives than ingredients.
They called it eco. The plastic water bottles disagreed.

title: More mistakes worth skipping
intro: New, to add to the five on the About page. Two lean on your own history (marked); keep those only if they ring true.

items.line: Skipping travel insurance. | Antarctica, 2020, taught me that one. Ask me how long 'a few extra days' can last.
items.check: Uses your COVID shutdown in Antarctica

items.line: Driving a road you don't know after dark. | Costa Rica in the nineties cured me of that.
Ignoring the tide table. | The ocean doesn't read your itinerary.
Closing the bar before a 5:30 game drive. | The leopard won't wait while you find your hat.
Going in the wrong season to save money. | The rain is cheaper for a reason.
Treating the guide like a driver. | He's the reason you came. Ask questions.
Trying to tick off the Big Five by lunch. | Africa isn't a checklist. It's a conversation.
Booking the cheapest flight to save one night's rate. | You'll spend the savings in a transit lounge.
Packing for every possible occasion. | Half the clothes, twice the sunscreen.
Planning the honeymoon around someone else's photos. | Pick the place that suits you two, not the feed.

title: Words we strike out
intro: New. The house style crosses these out in the margin with your reason. Pick the ones you'd actually cross out.

items.line: Bucket list | Trips aren't chores to finish before you die. Go because you're alive.
Hidden gem | If it's on Instagram, it isn't hidden. If it's a gem, we won't shout about it.
Bespoke | That's for suits. We design journeys.
Curated | Museums curate. We've slept there.
Off the beaten path | Someone beat it. Usually us, first.
Once in a lifetime | Africa will call you back. Plan for twice.
Unforgettable | You be the judge. After.
Five-star | Stars are for hotels. We count guides, silence and breakfast.
Paradise | Every island says so. Few have the reef to prove it.
Authentic experience | If you have to say it, it isn't.
Wanderlust | That's a tattoo, not a plan.
Seamless | Travel has seams. We know where they are.

title: Sign-off lines
intro: New options for the rotating line that closes each verdict. The seven approved ones stay.

items.line: Go early. The animals don't sleep in.
Bring a good book. You won't read it.
The detour is the trip.
Book the extra night. You'll thank me on the second morning.
Check the tide, then check out.
Less schedule. More story.
Ask the locals. Tip the guide.
Leave room in the bag and the calendar.
If it's not worth the bumpy road, it's not in the Ledger.
Sunscreen, curiosity, an open Tuesday.

title: Lines in your hand
intro: New short lines for the handwritten JW postmark on stay pages without a personal verdict.

items.line: Trust the guide. JW

Worth the bumpy road. JW
Tide first. JW

Long lens, short schedule. JW
Sit still. It comes to you. JW
Ask for the corner. JW
Pack light, stay late. JW
Sundowners are mandatory. JW
